cards.name: bilinear_rank_resynthesis_karatsuba
cards.identity: Detect that a whole Toffoli-level segment realizes a BILINEAR F2 map y_k ^= B_k(a,b) on three disjoint registers: A (read-only), B (read-only), Y (targets). Extraction: each 'h t; ccz(x1,y1,t) ... ccz(xm,ym,t); h t' group equals the classical update t ^= (x1&y1 ^ ... ^ xm&ym) (the CCZs commute, and H.CZ(t,f).H = CX(f,t)); propagate these updates plus the plain cx gates symbolically over the F2 polynomial ring in the A,B variables, giving for each y_k a bilinear form B_k = sum_{i,j} M_k[i][j] a_i b_j. The naive cost is 4 T per distinct monomial a_i b_j (one AND gadget each). Instead compute a RANK decomposition of the shared bilinear tensor: find R rank-1 terms P_r = (u_r . a)(v_r . b), u_r, v_r in F2^n, and F2 coefficients c_{k,r} with B_k = sum_r c_{k,r} P_r. Emit: for each r, CX the bits of u_r into ancilla p and v_r into ancilla q (free Clifford), AND-compute p&q -> ancilla s (Gidney gadget, 4 T), cx/cz s into every y_k with c_{k,r}=1, measured-uncompute s (0 T), then undo the two CX fan-ins; ancillas are reused across r. Cost 4R T. For mult_4 the extracted map is GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1: q8=c0^c4, q9=c1^c4^c5, q10=c2^c5^c6, q11=c3^c6 with c_k = sum_{i+j=k} a_i b_j, 16 monomials -> 64 T today. Karatsuba gives R=9: with A0=a0+a1x, A1=a2+a3x, B0=b0+b1x, B1=b2+b3x, P0=a0b0, P1=a1b1, P2=(a0^a1)(b0^b1), P3=a2b2, P4=a3b3, P5=(a2^a3)(b2^b3), u0=a0^a2, u1=a1^a3, v0=b0^b2, v1=b1^b3, P6=u0v0, P7=u1v1, P8=(u0^u1)(v0^v1); then A0B0 = P0 + (P0^P1^P2)x + P1x^2, A1B1 = P3 + (P3^P4^P5)x + P4x^2, M = (A0+A1)(B0+B1) = P6 + (P6^P7^P8)x + P7x^2, and a*b = A0B0 + (M + A0B0 + A1B1)x^2 + A1B1 x^4; finally reduce with x^4 = x+1, x^5 = x^2+x, x^6 = x^3+x^2 (all XOR = CX). Implementation note: for the general trigger, obtain R by table lookup of the known optimal bilinear decompositions for n-bit F2 polynomial multiplication (n<=4: R = 1,3,6,9) when the extracted tensor matches a polynomial-multiplication pattern, and otherwise by a bounded F2 rank search; if no decomposition with R < #monomials is found, do not fire.
cards.correctness: Two independent steps, each exact over F2. (1) Extraction is an identity of unitaries: a group of CCZs sharing target t contributes phase (-1)^{t*(sum_k x_k y_k)}; the exponent is mod 2, so the group equals CZ(t, f) with f = XOR_k (x_k & y_k), and conjugating by H on t turns it into t ^= f. Since A and B are never written anywhere in the segment, all such updates commute and the segment is exactly the classical reversible map y -> y ^ M(a,b), linear in y and bilinear in (a,b); the symbolic F2 propagation computes M exactly. (2) The replacement computes the same M: each P_r = (u_r.a)(v_r.b) is produced exactly by the AND gadget (Gidney 2018: compute |a AND b> with 4 T and a clean ancilla; uncompute by X-basis measurement of the ancilla plus a classically controlled CZ, exactly, 0 T), and B_k = sum_r c_{k,r} P_r is the defining property of the rank decomposition, verified symbolically over F2 before emission (and, for the Karatsuba instance, it is the standard Karatsuba identity (A0+A1x^2)(B0+B1x^2) = A0B0 + ((A0+A1)(B0+B1)+A0B0+A1B1)x^2 + A1B1x^4 applied twice, plus reduction mod x^4+x+1, which holds identically over F2[x]). All linear combination steps are CX (Clifford, exact) and are undone, so the two ancillas used for fan-in and the one AND-result ancilla start and end in |0>. Phase consistency is immediate: every emitted non-Clifford element is inside AND gadgets whose branch-dependent phases are cancelled by the classically controlled fix-up, so each measurement branch applies the same c_m = 1 to every input; hence the relaxed spec check (function + ancillas restored + phase consistency) is the right contract.
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit. (a) Partition the op list into maximal H-sandwiched groups on each target wire; require every non-Clifford gate to be ccz/ccx and every group to have the form h t; (ccz with target t)*; h t (or ccx directly), with the two controls of each ccz/ccx drawn from a set A_union_B of wires that are never a target of any gate in the segment, and the gate targets drawn from a disjoint wire set Y; the only other allowed gates on Y are cx/x/cz among Y wires. (b) Split A_union_B into A, B such that every ccz/ccx has one control in A and one in B (bipartite check on the control-pair graph; for mult_4 A = q0..q3, B = q4..q7, Y = q8..q11). (c) Symbolically propagate to get M_k, the bilinear form on each y_k in Y. (d) Count distinct monomials m (16 here) and obtain a rank decomposition with R < m (9 here, from the GF(2)-polynomial-multiplication pattern match on the Hankel/anti-diagonal structure of the monomial sets, i.e. M_k is a XOR of the anti-diagonals c_k of the outer product a b^T with the reduction folding). Fire once on the whole segment; emit the new segment with up to 3 appended clean ancillas.
cards.expected_effect: All 16 ccz gates and the 14 H gates disappear, replaced by 9 AND gadgets (4 T each = 36 T) plus CX fan-in/fan-out and the mod-x^4+x+1 XOR reduction (Clifford only), with 3 clean ancillas (12 -> 15 qubits) and 9 measurements with classically controlled CZ fix-ups. T: 64 -> 36. CNOT count rises by roughly 60-80 (lexicographically irrelevant since T drops). This beats every baseline on this circuit (TKET 96, pyzx/T-par 68, BQSKit 112) and also the best phase-polynomial result known for GF(2^4)-mult (TODD, 56 T), because the saving comes from the bilinear RANK of the map (9) rather than from the number of cubic phase-polynomial terms.
cards.source: Karatsuba & Ofman 1962 (and Karatsuba for F2[x]; bilinear complexity 9 for 4x4 F2 polynomial multiplication); Kepley & Steinwandt, 'Quantum circuits for F_{2^n}-multiplication with subquadratic gate count', Quantum Inf. Process. 14 (2015); Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2 (2018) (4-T AND with measurement-based uncompute); benchmark context: Amy, Maslov, Mosca T-par and Heyfron & Campbell TODD 2018, which report 68 and 56 T for GF(2^4)-mult.

cards.name: quadratic_and_count_minimization_over_f2
cards.identity: Reuse the (already implemented) Toffoli-level extraction that turns an H-sandwiched CCZ/CCX segment into a classical F2 update y_k ^= Q_k(a,b) on disjoint read-only registers A, B and target register Y (each group 'h t; ccz(x_i,y_i,t)*; h t' equals t ^= XOR_i (x_i & y_i), propagated symbolically together with the plain cx/x gates). Where the admitted rule then looks for a BILINEAR rank decomposition Q_k = sum_r c_{k,r} (u_r.a)(v_r.b) and pays 4 T per rank-1 term, this rule searches the strictly larger class of QUADRATIC (non-bilinear) straight-line F2 programs: a program is a sequence of R AND steps s_r = L_r(a,b,s_1..s_{r-1}) & L'_r(a,b,s_1..s_{r-1}) with L, L' arbitrary AFFINE forms over all input bits AND all previously computed AND results, followed by affine output forms Q_k = A_k(a,b,s_1..s_R). Two features of F2 make this class strictly stronger than the bilinear one: (i) squaring is linear, x^2 = x, so an AND of two forms that both mix A and B expands as L&L' = (bilinear part) XOR (affine self-terms from x_i^2 = x_i) XOR (unwanted a_i a_j / b_i b_j cross terms); the affine self-terms are FREE (they are absorbed into the final affine output forms, i.e. into cx/x gates), and only the genuine a_i a_j, b_i b_j cross terms must cancel across the R steps; (ii) feeding an AND output back into a later AND input produces degree-3+ intermediates that a bilinear algorithm cannot use, and these can also cancel. Hence the proven-optimal bilinear count for a map is only an upper bound here, not a floor. Procedure: (1) extract the tensor T_{ijk} / the forms Q_k; (2) compute the bilinear rank R0 by the existing path (9 for GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, the mult_4 map); (3) run a bounded exact search for a quadratic program with R = R0-1 AND steps: encode the unknown affine coefficient vectors of L_r, L'_r and of the output forms A_k as F2 unknowns, and the requirement 'program output == Q_k identically as polynomials' as an F2 polynomial-identity system; solve it with a SAT/CP search over the coefficient bits (sympy / pure-python DPLL is enough at this size: for mult_4, R=8, 8 variables of width <= 8+r each, with the standard symmetry breaking -- fix the affine part of L_1, order the steps lexicographically, and fix the free self-term coefficients to 0 in the output forms since they are absorbed anyway), with a hard node/time budget; (4) if a program is found, VERIFY it symbolically over the F2 polynomial ring against the extracted Q_k, then emit it: for each AND step, CX/X the affine form L_r into clean ancilla p and L'_r into clean ancilla q (Clifford, free), Gidney AND-compute p&q -> clean ancilla s_r (4 T), keep s_r alive only as long as a later step or output form needs it, measured-uncompute s_r (0 T), undo the fan-ins; finally emit the affine output forms as cx/x into Y. Cost 4R T. (5) If no program with R < R0 is found inside the budget, do not fire (the admitted bilinear rule keeps its result); if one is found, this rule supersedes it on that segment.
cards.correctness: Three independent exact steps. (1) Extraction is an identity of unitaries, unchanged from the admitted rule: a group of CCZs sharing target t imposes phase (-1)^{t . XOR_i (x_i y_i)} = CZ(t, f) with f = XOR_i (x_i & y_i), and H.CZ(t,f).H = CX(f,t); since A and B are never written in the segment all updates commute, so the segment is exactly the classical map y -> y XOR Q(a,b). (2) The replacement program is checked to compute the SAME map by symbolic identity over F2[a_0..a_{n-1}, b_0..b_{m-1}]: the candidate program is evaluated as polynomials with x_i^2 reduced to x_i (the correct reduction, since every variable is a bit, i.e. we work in the Boolean quotient ring F2[x]/(x_i^2 - x_i), which is exactly the ring of Boolean functions), and the resulting output polynomials must be equal coefficientwise to Q_k. This check is what makes the non-bilinear self-terms sound: they are real contributions to the polynomial and are either cancelled by other steps or cancelled by the affine output forms, and the identity check sees them. Nothing is accepted on the basis of the search encoding alone. (3) Each emitted primitive is exact: CX/X fan-in of an affine form is Clifford; the Gidney AND gadget (Quantum 2 (2018)) computes |p AND q> on a clean ancilla with 4 T gates, and its uncomputation is an X-basis measurement of the ancilla plus a classically controlled CZ, exact and 0 T; all fan-ins are undone, so every ancilla starts and ends in |0>. Phase consistency (invariant 2): the only non-Clifford elements are inside AND gadgets whose branch-dependent phase is exactly cancelled by the classically controlled fix-up, so every measurement branch applies the same c_m = 1 to all inputs and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; hence the relaxed specification check (function + ancillas restored + phase consistency) is the correct contract. Because the AND steps may now be nested, the ancilla lifetimes are computed from the program's data dependencies and each ancilla is uncomputed in reverse order of its last use, which keeps the 'clean in, clean out' property.
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit. (a) Same segment detection as the admitted bilinear rule: maximal H-sandwiched CCZ/CCX groups, every non-Clifford gate a ccz/ccx whose controls lie in a wire set X that is never written in the segment, targets in a disjoint set Y whose only other gates are cx/x/cz among Y wires. (b) Symbolically propagate to the Boolean forms Q_k on each y_k in Y (degree 2 in the X variables here, but the rule does not require bilinearity or a bipartite A/B split -- that relaxation is part of the point, so it also fires on segments the bilinear rule rejects). (c) Compute the baseline count R0 = the number of AND gadgets the current book would use on this segment (bilinear rank if the bipartite split exists, else distinct monomials). (d) Run the bounded quadratic-program search for R = R0 - 1, then R0 - 2, under a fixed node/time budget. (e) Fire once on the whole segment only if a symbolically verified program with R < R0 exists; emit with up to 2 + (max live AND results) appended clean ancillas. On mult_4 the segment is the whole circuit, X = q0..q7, Y = q8..q11, Q = GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, R0 = 9.
cards.expected_effect: On mult_4 the 9 Gidney AND gadgets of the current (Karatsuba, bilinear-rank-9) implementation are replaced by R < 9 AND gadgets, each 4 T, with the extra affine corrections and the a_i a_j / b_i b_j cancellation terms costing only cx/x gates. The exhaustive bilinear search (Barbulescu-Detrey-Estibals-Zimmermann) proves 9 is optimal among BILINEAR formulae for GF(2^4) multiplication, so this is the only remaining direction: the quadratic class is not covered by that bound because over F2 the squaring map is linear and because AND outputs may be re-multiplied. Realistic outcome R = 8: T 36 -> 32 (and qubits rise by at most 1-2 over the current 15, CNOT count rises by roughly 20-40, both lexicographically below T). If the search closes R = 8 as infeasible it does not fire and nothing regresses; if it reaches R = 7 the gain doubles to 8 T. Secondary value: the same pass is the general AND-count minimizer for every other dv_recon target (adder_8, mcx_10, modred_21), where the current book uses one 4-T AND per Toffoli run and no rank/quadratic reduction has been attempted at all.

cards.name: and_program_lifting_with_complete_multiplicative_complexity_search
cards.identity: Operate on the form the circuit ALREADY has after the book fires, i.e. on a segment of and_compute/and_uncompute gadgets plus Clifford (cx/x/cz/h), not on raw ccz/h groups. (1) LIFT: scan the segment and build an F2 straight-line program. Maintain for every wire w a Boolean polynomial val(w) in the quotient ring F2[v]/(v_i^2 - v_i) over the segment's input variables v (one per wire live at segment entry). cx(c,t): val(t) += val(c); x(t): val(t) += 1; and_compute(p,q -> s) on a clean ancilla s: val(s) = val(p)*val(q), and record the AND step (val(p), val(q)); and_uncompute(s) with its classically controlled cz/cx fix-up: val(s) = 0 and the step's result becomes dead after its last linear use; cz/z/s/h are tracked as in the book's existing extraction (an H-sandwiched group on a wire whose polynomial is independent of that wire is the usual 't ^= f' update). The lift succeeds only if every val(w) is a well-defined polynomial, no measurement outcome feeds anything but the documented fix-ups, and every ancilla ends with val = 0. The result is: R0 AND steps, and output polynomials Q_k = val(y_k) for the wires y_k that changed. On mult_4 after bilinear_rank_resynthesis_karatsuba this lift returns R0 = 9 AND steps and Q = GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, with 36 T = 4*R0. (2) SEARCH for a program with R < R0 AND steps in the FULL multiplicative-complexity class, which is strictly larger than both classes tried before: step r is s_r = L_r * L'_r where L_r, L'_r are arbitrary AFFINE forms over (all segment input wires INCLUDING the target wires y, all previous results s_1..s_{r-1}, and 1); the outputs are Q_k = A_k(v, s_1..s_R) with A_k affine. Encode 'the program's output polynomials equal Q_k identically in F2[v]/(v_i^2-v_i)' as a CNF over the unknown coefficient bits of L_r, L'_r, A_k (the polynomial coefficients of each step are multilinear in the unknowns; introduce one Tseitin variable per monomial of each intermediate) and give it to a COMPLETE DPLL/CDCL solver written over stdlib, with symmetry breaking (fix L_1 up to the affine group action, order steps lexicographically, force the constant terms of the A_k to 0 since x gates are free) and a hard conflict budget. Try R = R0-1, then R0-2. (3) If SAT: re-expand the witness symbolically, check equality with Q_k coefficientwise, and only then emit: per step, CX/X the affine forms into two clean ancillas p, q, and_compute(p,q -> s_r) [4 T], keep s_r until its last use (dependencies computed from the program DAG), and_uncompute in reverse order of last use [0 T], undo the fan-ins; finally emit the affine output forms as cx/x into the y wires. Maintain for every wire w a Boolean polynomial val(w) in the quotient ring F2[v]/(v_i^2 - v_i) over the segment's input variables v (one per wire live at segment entry). cx(c,t): val(t) += val(c); x(t): val(t) += 1; and_compute(p,q -> s) on a clean ancilla s: val(s) = val(p)*val(q), and record the AND step (val(p), val(q)); and_uncompute(s) with its classically controlled cz/cx fix-up: val(s) = 0 and the step's result becomes dead after its last linear use; cz/z/s/h are tracked as in the book's existing extraction (an H-sandwiched group on a wire whose polynomial is independent of that wire is the usual 't ^= f' update). The lift succeeds only if every val(w) is a well-defined polynomial, no measurement outcome feeds anything but the documented fix-ups, and every ancilla ends with val = 0. The result is: R0 AND steps, and output polynomials Q_k = val(y_k) for the wires y_k that changed. On mult_4 after bilinear_rank_resynthesis_karatsuba this lift returns R0 = 9 AND steps and Q = GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, with 36 T = 4*R0. (2) SEARCH for a program with R < R0 AND steps in the FULL multiplicative-complexity class, which is strictly larger than both classes tried before: step r is s_r = L_r * L'_r where L_r, L'_r are arbitrary AFFINE forms over (all segment input wires INCLUDING the target wires y, all previous results s_1..s_{r-1}, and 1); the outputs are Q_k = A_k(v, s_1..s_R) with A_k affine. Three freedoms beyond the bilinear-rank class: free XOR with x^2 = x (a factor may mix a, b and y, and the self-terms it produces are absorbed by the affine output forms), AND-result feedback (degree >= 3 intermediates), and y-dependent factors whose spurious y-degree-2 contributions must cancel across steps. Encode 'the program's output polynomials equal Q_k identically in F2[v]/(v_i^2-v_i)' as a CNF over the unknown coefficient bits of L_r, L'_r, A_k (the polynomial coefficients of each step are multilinear in the unknowns; introduce one Tseitin variable per monomial of each intermediate) and give it to a COMPLETE DPLL/CDCL solver written over stdlib, with symmetry breaking (fix L_1 up to the affine group action, order steps lexicographically, force the constant terms of the A_k to 0 since x gates are free) and a hard conflict budget. Try R = R0-1, then R0-2. (3) If SAT: re-expand the witness symbolically, check equality with Q_k coefficientwise, and only then emit: per step, CX/X the affine forms into two clean ancillas p, q, and_compute(p,q -> s_r) [4 T], keep s_r until its last use (dependencies computed from the program DAG), and_uncompute in reverse order of last use [0 T], undo the fan-ins; finally emit the affine output forms as cx/x into the y wires. Cost 4R T. If UNSAT at R0-1 with the budget not exhausted, the book's program is proved optimal in this class: do not fire. If the budget is exhausted, do not fire.
cards.correctness: Three exact stages. (i) The lift is a sound abstraction, not a rewrite: and_compute on a clean ancilla puts exactly |val(p) AND val(q)> on that ancilla (Gidney 2018), cx/x act exactly as the affine updates on the computational basis, and every tracked wire therefore carries exactly the Boolean function val(w) on every basis input. Since the segment's only non-Clifford elements are AND gadgets and every ancilla is uncomputed, the segment IS the classical reversible map v -> (v with y_k replaced by Q_k(v)) up to a global phase and up to measurement-branch fix-ups that the gadget cancels; if any check in the lift fails the rule returns no match, so a lift bug can only cause a non-fire. (ii) The replacement is accepted only after a symbolic identity check in F2[v]/(v_i^2 - v_i), the ring of Boolean functions (correct because every wire carries a bit, so squaring is the identity): expand the candidate program's outputs as polynomials and require coefficientwise equality with the lifted Q_k. This is what makes the non-bilinear freedoms sound: self-terms from x^2 = x and spurious a_i a_j / b_i b_j / y-mixing terms are genuine polynomial contributions, and the check sees them, so they must truly cancel (against other steps or the affine output forms) before anything is emitted. Nothing is accepted on the strength of the SAT encoding. (iii) Emission is exact gate by gate: affine fan-in by CX/X is Clifford and is undone, so each of the two factor ancillas starts and ends in |0>; and_compute uses 4 T on a clean ancilla and and_uncompute is an X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled CZ, exact and 0 T, so each s_r ancilla also starts and ends in |0>; nesting is handled by uncomputing in reverse order of last use, which preserves clean-in/clean-out for the whole DAG. Phase consistency (invariant 2) holds because every measurement's branch-dependent phase is exactly cancelled by its fix-up, so each branch applies the same c_m = 1 to every input and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; function + ancilla restoration + phase consistency is exactly the relaxed contract the judge checks.
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit. (a) Take the maximal segment whose gates are only and_compute / and_uncompute (with their classically controlled fix-ups) and cx/x/cz/z/s/h, such that the lift of (1) succeeds: every and_compute target is a clean ancilla, every ancilla is uncomputed inside the segment, the H's occur only as sandwiches around groups on a wire whose polynomial does not involve that wire, and no measurement outcome is used outside its own fix-up. The segment may also be the raw ccz/ccx form (the lift treats an H-sandwiched ccz group as t ^= XOR_i x_i y_i), so the rule fires whether or not the book's bilinear rule has already run -- this is the concrete difference from the two earlier cards, which could only read raw ccz segments and therefore never matched once bilinear_rank_resynthesis_karatsuba had consumed the ccz/h structure (history attempt 2: 'trigger matched on none of the 10 suite runs'). (b) Require R0 = #AND steps >= 2 and at least one changed output wire. (c) Run the complete search at R = R0-1 and R0-2 under a fixed conflict/time budget. (d) Fire once on the segment only if a symbolically verified program with R < R0 is found; up to 2 + max-live-results clean ancillas are appended. cards.expected_effect: mult_4 currently spends all 36 T as 9 Gidney AND gadgets at 4 T; there is no other non-Clifford cost in the circuit, so the only possible gain is a program with fewer AND steps. Finding R = 8 gives T 36 -> 32 (qubits 15 -> at most 16, CNOTs +20..40, both lexicographically below T); R = 7 would give 28. The reason to expect R = 8 to be reachable here where the earlier seeded-TODD and bilinear searches found nothing: the proven lower bound of 9 (Barbulescu-Detrey-Estibals-Zimmermann) is a BILINEAR rank bound, the search here is complete rather than move-based, and the class now also admits affine factors that mix the target register y and AND-result feedback, which no earlier attempt encoded. The honest downside is symmetric and cheap: if the solver returns UNSAT at R = 8 the rule does not fire, nothing regresses, and the book's 36 T is then proved optimal in the multiplicative-complexity class, which settles this circuit. Secondary value on the rest of the dv_recon suite: the same lift reads the post-rewrite adder_8 / mcx_10 / modred_21 circuits, where the book emits one 4-T AND per Toffoli run and no AND-count minimization has ever been applied to the lifted program.

cards.name: in_place_affine_routing_for_and_gadget_fanin
cards.identity: Emit the factors of every AND gadget IN PLACE on the read-only registers instead of on dedicated fan-in ancillas. Operate on the form the circuit already has after the book fires: a segment containing R and_compute(p_r, q_r -> s_r) gadgets, where p_r and q_r are clean ancillas that are loaded with affine forms by CX/X gates from source wires and then unloaded again around each gadget, s_r is CX/CZ'd into targets, and and_uncompute(s_r) closes the gadget. Extraction: from the CX/X fan-in read off, for each r, the F2 affine forms u_r . a (on p_r) and v_r . b (on q_r), where A and B are the sets of source wires feeding the first and second factor (disjoint; wires never written inside the segment). Replacement: pick one wire a* in A and one b* in B, and keep exactly ONE clean ancilla s. Maintain a running invertible F2 matrix (basis) on the A wires and one on the B wires, both initially the identity. For product r, emit the CNOT network (Patel-Markov-Hayes / Gaussian elimination, CX gates among A wires only) realizing L_r . L_{r-1}^{-1}, where L_r is any invertible map on A whose a*-row is u_r (every nonzero u_r extends to an invertible matrix); same on B with v_r. Then emit and_compute(a*, b* -> s) [4 T], re-emit the gadget's original downstream CX/CZ from s into the targets unchanged, and and_uncompute(s) [0 T]. Proceed to r+1 by composing the next elimination network (no unload/reload). After the last product emit L_R^{-1} on A and the corresponding inverse on B, restoring both registers exactly. Order the products to minimise the elimination cost between consecutive forms (greedy nearest-neighbour / Gray-code over the multiset {(u_r, v_r)}). The two fan-in ancillas are then dead and are dropped: qubit count falls by 2. Fire only if the T-count is unchanged and the qubit count strictly drops.
cards.correctness: Every step is an exact Clifford identity plus an unchanged gadget. (i) The elimination networks consist of CX gates acting only on A wires (resp. only on B wires), which are never written anywhere else in the segment, so they implement exactly the invertible linear map L_r on the A register and nothing else; because the final emitted network is L_R^{-1}, the composition of all networks over the segment is the identity, so the A and B registers hold their original values at the segment exit (and, if any non-fan-in gate inside the segment reads an A or B wire, the rule inserts the restoring inverse before it, so such reads see the original basis too). (ii) At gadget r the wire a* carries exactly the bit u_r . a and b* carries exactly v_r . b, i.e. the SAME bit values that the deleted fan-in ancillas p_r, q_r carried at that point; and_compute therefore writes the same product bit onto s (Gidney 2018: |p AND q> on a clean ancilla with 4 T), and the downstream CX/CZ into the targets are re-emitted verbatim, so the classical function computed by the segment is unchanged. (iii) and_uncompute is an X-basis measurement of s plus a classically controlled CZ on its two input wires; applying it to (a*, b*) instead of (p_r, q_r) is the same gadget on wires holding the same bits, so its branch-dependent phase is cancelled exactly as before: every measurement branch applies the same c_m = 1 to every input and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. (iv) s is clean before each gadget and restored to |0> by the uncompute, and the two dropped ancillas were clean-in/clean-out and are no longer touched, so ancilla restoration holds. Hence function correctness + ancilla restoration + phase consistency, exactly the relaxed contract; the unitary part is exact up to global phase. A bug in the basis bookkeeping can only make the rule not fire (the matrices are tracked symbolically and the final composition is checked to be the identity before emission).
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit. (a) Find a maximal segment whose non-Clifford content is only and_compute / and_uncompute gadgets with their classically controlled fix-ups, the rest being cx/x/cz/h. (b) Require, for each gadget, that both and_compute inputs are ancilla wires that are |0> at segment entry, whose only other gates in the segment are CX/X from a set S of wires that are never a target of any gate in the segment, and whose fan-in is undone before the next gadget (so the ancilla is clean again). (c) Compute each gadget's two affine forms by symbolic F2 propagation of that fan-in; require the supports of the first factors (set A) and of the second factors (set B) to be disjoint subsets of S, each with at least one wire, and every form to be nonzero. (d) Require at least two gadgets and at least two distinct fan-in ancillas to eliminate. (e) Fire once on the segment, emitting the in-place form with a single AND-result ancilla; accept only if T is unchanged and qubits strictly drop. On mult_4 this matches the segment produced by bilinear_rank_resynthesis_karatsuba: R = 9 gadgets, A = {q0..q3}, B = {q4..q7}, targets q8..q11, two fan-in ancillas plus one result ancilla.
cards.expected_effect: T is untouched by design: the 9 and_compute gadgets stay, 36 T. The gain is on the next lexicographic keys. Qubits: 15 -> 13 (the two fan-in ancillas p, q disappear; only the AND-result ancilla remains). CNOT: the current form pays |u_r| + |v_r| CX to load plus the same to unload around every product (roughly 8 CX per product, ~70 over the segment, plus the reduction XORs); the in-place form pays only the Gaussian-elimination cost between consecutive forms, which for the 9 Karatsuba forms on A ({a0, a1, a0+a1, a2, a3, a2+a3, a0+a2, a1+a3, a0+a1+a2+a3}, and the mirror set on B) is 1-2 CX per register per product under the greedy ordering, plus one restoring network, so roughly 30-35 CX in total: a drop of ~35-40. I state the T estimate as 0 deliberately: 9 Toffolis / ANDs is the frontier for GF(2^4) multiplication (Barbulescu et al.: bilinear complexity of F_16 over F_2 is 9, proven optimal by exhaustive search; AlphaTensor-Quantum reports exactly 9 Toffoli gadgets for the 12-qubit GF(2^4)-mult benchmark, and the two earlier attempts here searched the strictly larger quadratic / cubic-phase-polynomial classes and found nothing below 9), and no construction is known with fewer than 4 T per measured AND, so 36 T is not beatable on this circuit and the only admissible improvement left is the resource one. The rule is generic: it cuts two ancillas and a fan-in/unload pair out of every future product-emitting rule, and out of any dv_recon segment (adder_8, mcx_10, modred_21) whose gadgets are fed through fan-in ancillas.
cards.source: Patel, Markov & Hayes, 'Optimal synthesis of linear reversible circuits', QIC 8 (2008) (CNOT synthesis of an invertible F2 map in place on a register); Kepley & Steinwandt, 'Quantum circuits for F_{2^n}-multiplication with subquadratic gate count', QIP 14 (2015) (in-place routing of the linear forms of a Karatsuba multiplier rather than onto fan-in ancillas); Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2 (2018) (4-T AND gadget with measurement-based uncomputation); frontier references for the unbeatable T side: Barbulescu, Detrey, Estibals & Zimmermann, WAIFI 2012 (bilinear complexity of F_{2^4} = 9) and Ruiz et al., 'Quantum Circuit Optimization with AlphaTensor' (arXiv:2402.14396), which reports 9 Toffolis on this exact GF(2^4)-mult benchmark.
